items.title: The Rise and Fall of Our Ascent
items.petal:
There is a moment when you realise you are rising.

You feel lighter. The mind becomes quieter. And then, without noticing, you begin to fall. Not suddenly. Just a little less meditation, a little more ego, a little more attention on the world outside.

In Sahaja Yoga, Self-Realisation is not the destination. It is the beginning of our ascent. And we don't have to fight our way back: we return to meditation, and allow the Kundalini to do the work.

Rise. Fall. Watch. Correct. Grow.

How quickly do you notice that you have fallen, and turn back towards the centre?

items.title: The Left Side: How Do We Overcome It?
items.petal:
The past can be a teacher. It doesn't have to be your home.

In Sahaja Yoga, the Left Side is our emotional world: memories, desires, feelings. In balance, it gives us sensitivity and compassion. Too caught in it, we circle guilt, worry and nostalgia.

The way out isn't to fight those thoughts. It's to notice them, bring attention back to the present, and turn outwards: meditate together, help someone, ask “What can I give?”

Don't deny your emotions. Witness them.

Where is your attention living today: in the past, or here?

items.title: This moment is going to transform your life
items.petal:
What if a quiet upgrade of human awareness is already under way?

From a fellow meditator, this 2016 post shares a 1985 talk by Shri Mataji in San Diego. Watched with a relaxed, open mind, it invites the gentle awakening of the Kundalini, felt as a cool breeze above the head or on the palms.

Its idea: meditation needn't stay an activity squeezed into a busy day. Through the Kundalini, it can become a state we live in.

No membership. No subscription. Freely available to everyone, everywhere.

Could you watch with an open mind, and simply notice what you feel?

items.title: The Cow, the flute and a Native American prophecy
items.petal:
A fellow meditator remembers arriving in New York with friends from London, just after midday on 15 June 1999.

After a public programme, the group travelled upstate to Canajoharie, farmland Shri Mataji had chosen from a small newspaper advertisement because, she said, its vibrations were “just shooting out”.

Stories spread that the land had been a last refuge for Native Americans. Next morning, a couple of them reported sensing braves on horseback, who seemed to approve and let them be.

Reverence for Mother Earth, it seemed, was something they shared.

Have you ever felt that a place itself was sacred?

items.title: Why do we dream? Q&A with Shri Mataji
items.petal:
Why do we dream?

In 1980, at Dollis Hill in London, someone put that question to Shri Mataji. In deep sleep, she said, our attention touches the unconscious, but on the way back the message gets clouded. So most dreams are confused. After Self-Realisation, they can become clearer.

Yet she advised against analysing dreams too much.

“The dreams are coming to you to give you a solution of a problem.”

When has a dream ever helped you find your way?

items.title: Spiritual food: chickpeas and vibrations
items.petal:
Could something as small as a chickpea carry vibrations?

In a New Year talk in India in 1978, Shri Mataji spoke of beauty that perishes, and the eternal forms behind it. Then, holding the chana she had been given to eat, she said its shape was among the best for vibrations.

Those who are sensitive, she said, can feel which things emit vibrations: incense, lamps, simple foods. So find the things of proper vibrations, and use them.

Small things that look insignificant can be of very great power.

What small, ordinary thing in your home brings you peace?

items.title: Human beings have to now become superhuman beings
items.petal:
“Today, we are standing at a point where we have to become superhuman beings.”

Speaking in Lille, France, in 1981, Shri Mataji described a power born within each of us, resting in the sacrum, the sacred bone. When it rises, she said, it is felt as a cool breeze on the head and hands.

You cannot pay for it or force it. Your freedom is absolutely respected. If you ask for it, you can have it.

It isn't about seeing something new. It's about becoming.

What might happen if you simply asked, with open hands?

items.title: Paramachaitanya: your miracle maker
items.petal:
What if the power behind everything is simply vibrations?

In this talk, Shri Mataji calls it Paramachaitanya: the all-pervading power that holds all knowledge, truth and light. We are made by it and surrounded by it all the time. We only get lost in its folds, through our own unawareness.

Once we become aware that we are part and parcel of it, she said, it acts, and it creates possibilities.

Ignorance is only the absence of light.

Where might you be lost in the folds, rather than resting in the ocean?

items.title: What is thoughtless awareness?
items.petal:
A thought rises and falls. Another rises and falls.

We live in the past or the future, dancing on the cusp of our thoughts. In talks in Sydney and Amsterdam, Shri Mataji explained that when the Kundalini rises, thoughts become lean, and a space opens between them: the present.

That space is thoughtless awareness. You are aware, but thoughtless. You can think if you want to. You don't have to.

The present lives in the gaps between our thoughts.

Could you give yourself five quiet minutes tomorrow morning?

items.title: Stonehenge, created by Mother Earth
items.petal:
Some places, Shri Mataji said, are created by Mother Earth herself.

In New York in 1983, she told of an Indian village where, a century earlier, an English engineer tried to build a tank. Whatever he built at one spot was gone by the next day. When she saw the place, she knew.

Stonehenge, she said, is the same story: a place that vibrates divinity and compassion. But only a realised soul can truly feel it.

Mother Earth has her own sacred places, waiting to be felt.

Where have you felt that the earth itself was speaking?
